subject: physics
question_text: For what angle of projection is the horizontal range of a projectile maximum? Write that maximum range.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The condition
lines: The range of a projectile is
u and g are fixed, so R is largest when
sin 2θ is largest, that is sin 2θ = 1.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Quote R = u² sin 2θ / g and state the condition sin 2θ = 1.
steps.why: The angle sits inside one sine, so the whole question is "when is a sine equal to 1". This mark stops at sin 2θ = 1; the value θ = 45° belongs to the next step.
common_mistakes: Maximising sin θ instead of sin 2θ, which gives 90° and zero range.

recall.must_convey: That R is u squared sin 2 theta by g, so R is maximum when sin 2 theta equals 1.
accept: u squared sin 2 theta by g

steps.memory_tip: The angle inside the sine is 2θ, not θ. Make sin 2θ as large as possible and nothing else.

steps.label: The angle and the range

lines.text: Maximum range = u² / g,  at θ = 45°

lines: The angle 45° does not depend on the
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both parts are wanted: the angle 45° and the range u²/g.
steps.why: 45° splits the speed equally between carrying the body forward and keeping it in the air, which is why 45° is the best angle at every speed.
common_mistakes: Writing the maximum range as u²/2g, which is the maximum HEIGHT of a vertical throw.

recall.must_convey: That theta is 45 degrees and the maximum range is u squared by g.

steps.memory_tip: 2θ = 90° means θ = 45°, so halve it. Then sin 90° = 1 leaves R = u²/g exactly.

insider_note: The condition sin 2θ = 1 is a full mark before the answer. θ = 45° with no working earns one mark, not two.
